props.statement: The team decided to categorize background events into ERROR and RECONCILIATION logical groups for clarity and simplicity.

statement.value: The team decided to categorize background events into ERROR and RECONCILIATION logical groups for clarity and simplicity.

n_bd3ce52d28ecbe2b1b3e5d0a5084a84e.value: I agree with keeping the logical groups as ERROR and RECONCILIATION. Based on your explanation and the current 6 BackgroundEvent.Type values, that split seems appropriate.

props.statement: Separating logical lanes based on when an event is allowed to be consumed (e.g., poll vs. unsubscribe) improves robustness over a single queue with filtering.

statement.value: Separating logical lanes based on when an event is allowed to be consumed (e.g., poll vs. unsubscribe) improves robustness over a single queue with filtering.

n_2ba0d4394557a0de85d5d57659590960.value: I think it would be more robust to separate logical lanes based on when an event is allowed to be consumed, rather than continuing with the current model where all events are placed into a single queue and the caller drains everything and then filters afterward.

props.title: Separate lanes for event consumption contexts

props.statement: The absence of consumption context in BackgroundEvent leads to fragile solutions like the skipAssignmentEvents flag.

statement.value: The absence of consumption context in BackgroundEvent leads to fragile solutions like the skipAssignmentEvents flag.

n_2ba0d4394557a0de85d5d57659590960.value: one issue that has been pointed out in several tickets is that a Background Event does not carry any information about when it is supposed to be consumed. The absence of that information is what leads us to introduce flags such as skipAssignmentEvents

props.title: Current BackgroundEvent lacks consumption context

props.statement: The team prioritizes keeping logical groups (e.g., errors, callbacks) clear rather than introducing broad abstractions like ConsumptionPolicy.

statement.value: The team prioritizes keeping logical groups (e.g., errors, callbacks) clear rather than introducing broad abstractions like ConsumptionPolicy.

n_7492b2da53e7982101de4a0e3f2584b6.value: I agree with your point about encapsulating the logic in the background event handler, good point, but worth aiming for not obfuscating the logical groups (errors, callbacks)

props.title: Keep logical groups clear over broad abstractions

props.statement: Supporting ByteBuffer as a value allows users to manage pooled/reused buffers more efficiently by allocating before send and releasing after, since data is copied to the accumulator immediately.

statement.value: Supporting ByteBuffer as a value allows users to manage pooled/reused buffers more efficiently by allocating before send and releasing after, since data is copied to the accumulator immediately.

n_4f4ee091d865322794f9e232bd2c804e.value: There appears to be more sense in explicit support for ByteBuffer as a value so that user code can allocate it before calling producer.send and release after that since it's guaranteed that the contents have been copied to producer's accumulator by then

props.title: ByteBuffer support rationale

props.statement: The mandatory 'value.serializer' property complicates ByteBuffer support because it is checked at KafkaProducer construction time, before any value is present.

statement.value: The mandatory 'value.serializer' property complicates ByteBuffer support because it is checked at KafkaProducer construction time, before any value is present.

n_4f4ee091d865322794f9e232bd2c804e.value: The only huccup here is that "value.serializer" property is mandatory and its presence is checked at KafkaProducer's contstruction time when there's no value present yet

props.title: Serializer property constraint

props.statement: One workaround is to keep the value serializer mandatory but ignore it if the value is a ByteBuffer, as its contents can be copied without serialization.

statement.value: One workaround is to keep the value serializer mandatory but ignore it if the value is a ByteBuffer, as its contents can be copied without serialization.

n_4f4ee091d865322794f9e232bd2c804e.value: The other option is to keep value serializer mandatory like now but ignore it if the value is a ByteBuffer whose contents can be copied without any serializers

props.title: Serializer workaround for ByteBuffer
